key_insight: AnimationBench is a benchmark tailored to animation-style video generation, showing that existing video evaluation suites fail to capture stylized appearance, exaggerated motion, and character-centric consistency in animated content.
problem_solved: Existing benchmarks are built for realistic videos and use fixed prompts and rigid pipelines, so they cannot reliably evaluate the unique challenges of animation-style generation—especially character identity, expressive motion, and style fidelity.
method: Introduce AnimationBench: a character-centric, animation-focused evaluation suite with diverse stylized examples and flexible prompt support for open-domain content.
Define evaluation targets and metrics that emphasize character consistency, exaggerated/expressive motion, and stylization fidelity (combining automated measures with human judgments).
Provide a flexible pipeline for customizable prompts and per-character evaluation to enable reproducible, fine-grained comparisons across models.
impact: AnimationBench gives researchers and practitioners a realistic, targeted way to measure progress on animated video generation, enabling development of models that better preserve character identity, expressive motion, and stylistic fidelity.
visual_elements: Side-by-side examples: ground-truth animated clip vs. model outputs annotated for character identity and style errors
Pipeline diagram: dataset + flexible prompt interface + automated + human evaluation loop
Bar chart or radar chart: metric-wise comparisons (character consistency, motion fidelity, style match) across models
Timeline/heatmap: per-frame character consistency over time to highlight identity drift
paper_title: AnimationBench: Are Video Models Good at Character-Centric Animation?
paper_authors: Leyi Wu, Pengjun Fang, Kai Sun, Yazhou Xing, Yinwei Wu
